threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the onboarding rollout.

messages.text: Welcome to the Hybrid Customer Onboarding Workspace Rollout project. We have 21 days to design and pilot a standardized onboarding process that works for both office and remote teams. This thread is for us to align on scope, success criteria, and the initial backlog. Let's start by confirming what we're building and what we're explicitly NOT building in this phase.

Good kickoff. I think we need to be clear on scope boundaries early. Are we redesigning the entire customer lifecycle, or just the first 30 days of onboarding? And do we include post-onboarding support handoff, or is that out of scope?

Excellent question. Scope is: first 30 days from contract signature to project kickoff. Handoff to project delivery is in scope; ongoing support is out. We'll document this in A1 as part of T1 and T2. Let me also flag that we need to map the current state first—I'll coordinate interviews with recent project owners to understand pain points.

I can help with the interviews—I've worked across sales and project teams, so I know the friction points. Also, we'll need to define what success looks like. Should we track cycle time, error rates, rework cycles? I'm thinking A4 should capture these KPIs clearly so we can measure pilot impact.

Agree. For D2, I'd suggest we track: (1) onboarding cycle time in days, (2) number of rework cycles per customer, (3) compliance errors caught before vs after pilot. These are measurable and directly tied to the risks we're mitigating.

Perfect. Let's lock that in for D2. I'll make sure T12 creates the tracking sheet with those three KPIs. Now, on the backlog: T1 (map current state) and T2 (design target workflow) are critical path. T3 and T7 (templates and checklists) depend on T2 being done. T4 (legal review) is parallel but must complete before pilot. Does this sequencing make sense to everyone?
I can start on T1 mapping. I'll reach out to a few project owners this week to understand the current flow. Should I also document the tools they're currently using, or just the steps?
Both—steps and tools. That'll help us understand what we can reuse and where we have gaps. Once you have the as-is documented, we'll move to T2 design. I'll coordinate with 119847 and 387705 on that.
One more thing on scope: are we including customer-facing onboarding materials in this rollout, or just internal process and workspace? I ask because that affects T3 and T5 complexity.

Good catch. For this phase, we're focusing on internal process and workspace. Customer-facing materials (welcome packets, etc.) are out of scope for the pilot—we'll use existing templates. This is part of D1. Let me summarize: scope is internal hybrid workflow, workspace structure, and templates for internal teams. Out of scope: customer-facing redesign, post-onboarding support, and tool procurement.

Clear. So D1 is locked: internal hybrid workflow, workspace, internal templates. D2 is locked: cycle time, rework cycles, compliance errors. Both decisions recorded. Next steps: 83011 starts T1 interviews this week, I'll prep for T2 design once T1 is ready. 14637, can you start drafting the KPI sheet structure for T12?
Yes, I'll draft T12 today. I'll include columns for customer name, start date, cycle time, rework count, and compliance flags. Should be ready for review by EOD.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the target onboarding workflow, RACI, and workspace structure.

messages.text: Sharing first draft of the to-be workflow and workspace proposal. I've incorporated feedback from T1 interviews and mapped out the target state in A1. The workflow has five main phases: intake, qualification, setup, kickoff, and handoff. Each phase has clear RACI assignments. Workspace structure is in A6—folder hierarchy follows the workflow phases to keep things organized.

Good start. I have a few questions on the RACI. In the 'setup' phase, who's accountable for ensuring legal docs are complete? Is that project management or legal? And for the workspace, are we using shared folders or channels, or both?

Good questions. In setup, project management is accountable for ensuring legal docs are complete—they own the checklist. Legal is consulted (C) and informed (I). For workspace, we're using both: shared folders for document storage (templates, contracts, etc.) and channels for team communication and status updates. This keeps documents organized and conversations threaded.

I'm reviewing the workspace structure from a technical feasibility angle. A6 proposes a naming convention like 'CUST-[CustomerName]-[Phase]'. That works, but we need to confirm IT can support the access control rules you've defined. I'd suggest we submit A8 (IT request) early so they have time to validate the setup before we configure the pilot workspace in T6.

Agreed. 95041, can you draft the IT request for A8 today? We need to specify: folder structure, access rules (who can read/write/delete), and any automation or integration needs. Once IT confirms feasibility, we can lock D3 and D4.

I'll draft A8 today. One thing to flag: if IT says they can't support the access control granularity we want, we may need to simplify the structure. I'll include a 'workaround' section in the request so we have a backup plan.

Smart. While 95041 is working on the IT request, I want to make sure the workspace structure is intuitive for users. Can we add a 'quick reference' section to A6 that shows where to find common items? Like 'where do I upload the contract?' or 'where do I post status updates?' That'll help with adoption.
Great idea. I'll add a 'quick reference' section to A6 with screenshots and examples. That ties into A2 (quick-start guide) as well—we can cross-reference them.

I have a question on the RACI for the 'intake' phase. Who's responsible for initial customer communication? Is that sales or project management? The current state is messy—sometimes sales owns it, sometimes project management jumps in early.

Good catch. In the target state, sales is responsible (R) for initial customer communication. Project management is consulted (C) on scope and timeline. This creates a clear handoff point. I'll update A1 to make this explicit.

Okay, so we have: workflow RACI in A1 (updated), workspace structure in A6 (with quick reference), and IT request in A8 (in progress). Before we lock D3 and D4, I want to make sure sales management has reviewed the RACI. Can someone reach out to them for sign-off?
I'll reach out to sales management tomorrow morning. I'll send them A1 with a summary of the RACI changes and ask for feedback by EOD. Once I have their sign-off, we can confirm D3.

I'll have A8 ready by EOD today. Once IT responds (hopefully by tomorrow), we can finalize the workspace structure and lock D4. The naming convention and folder hierarchy in A6 are solid, but we may need to adjust access rules based on IT feedback.

Good. So timeline: 119847 gets sales sign-off by EOD tomorrow, 95041 submits A8 today and follows up with IT. Once both are done, we lock D3 and D4, and we can move to T6 (configure pilot workspace). This keeps us on track for the 21-day deadline.

threads.thread_goal: Create and validate templates, checklists, and compliance aspects.

messages.text: Posting initial versions of templates and checklists for review. I've created A5 (template pack) with email and document templates for each workflow phase. A3 (internal checklists) has separate checklists for sales, project, and customer success teams. All templates follow the naming and structure conventions from A6. Ready for feedback.

Good work. I'm reviewing the templates now. One question: do the email templates include placeholders for customer-specific data (name, contract number, etc.)? And are there version control notes so teams know which version to use?

Yes, all email templates have placeholders like [CustomerName], [ContractNumber], [ProjectStartDate]. And I've added a version column in A5 so teams know which version is current. I also included a 'last updated' date and change notes.

Good. Now, the critical piece: legal and compliance review. T4 requires templates to be reviewed by legal before we use them in the pilot. 14637, have you already sent A5 and A3 to legal, or do we need to do that now?

Not yet. I wanted to get feedback from the team first. But I can send them to legal today. I'll include a cover note explaining the context and asking them to flag any data protection or compliance issues. Should I also ask them to review the checklists in A3, or just the templates in A5?
Both. The checklists reference data handling and compliance steps, so legal needs to review them too. Also, ask legal for a turnaround time—we need their sign-off before the pilot starts. This is D6.

Will do. I'll send A5 and A3 to legal today with a note asking for feedback by end of week. In the meantime, I'll also draft A2 (quick-start guide) so teams know how to use the templates and checklists. A2 will reference both A5 and A3.

Good plan. For A2, make sure to include: (1) which template to use for each workflow phase, (2) how to customize placeholders, (3) where to store completed documents, (4) escalation paths if something doesn't fit the template. That'll help with adoption.
Perfect. I'll include all of that in A2. I'll also add screenshots showing where to find templates in the workspace and how to use the checklists. Should be ready for review by tomorrow.

I have a question on the checklists. In A3, the project team checklist includes a step for 'confirm customer data protection agreement.' But I'm not sure what that means. Can you clarify what we're checking for?

Good catch. That step is about ensuring the customer has signed our data protection addendum before we start processing their data. I'll clarify that in A3 and add a reference to the template in A5. Legal will also review this when they check the templates.

Okay, so timeline: 14637 sends A5 and A3 to legal today, drafts A2 by tomorrow. Legal reviews by end of week. Once legal signs off, we can confirm D5 (templates approved) and D6 (compliance covered). Then we're ready for T6 (configure pilot workspace) and T9 (training).
One more thing: once legal approves, we should version-lock A5 and A3 so teams don't accidentally modify them. I'll add a note in A2 about this—templates are read-only until we decide to update them.

Good idea. I'll set up version control in the workspace so there's a clear 'current' version and an archive of previous versions. That way, if we need to update templates later, we have a clear change log.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate the pilot onboarding execution and training.

messages.text: Time to identify our first pilot customer and plan the pilot timeline. We need to select a customer that's representative but not too complex, so we can test the process without too much risk. Once we pick a customer, we'll schedule the pilot onboarding and coordinate training for internal teams. Let's discuss criteria for the pilot customer.

Good question. What makes a good pilot customer? I'd suggest: (1) medium-sized deal (not too small, not too large), (2) standard product/service (not heavily customized), (3) willing to provide feedback, (4) timeline allows us to complete onboarding within 2 weeks. Do we have any customers in the pipeline that fit?

I know of a customer—TechCorp—that signed a contract last week. They're a mid-sized tech company, standard implementation, and the sales rep mentioned they're eager to get started. They could start onboarding next week. Should I reach out to confirm they're willing to be a pilot?

Yes, please reach out to TechCorp and the sales rep. Confirm they're willing to be a pilot and that they can start onboarding next week. Also ask if they have a primary contact for the onboarding process. Once confirmed, we'll lock D7.

While 83011 is confirming TechCorp, I want to think about training. We need to train the internal teams on the new process before the pilot starts. Should we do a live session or recorded? And who needs to attend?

Good point. I'd suggest a live session for the pilot team (sales rep, project manager, customer success) so they can ask questions in real-time. Then a recorded session for the broader team. The live session should cover: (1) the new workflow, (2) how to use the workspace, (3) which templates to use, (4) escalation paths.

Agreed. So D8 is: live training session for pilot team, recorded session for broader team. 119847, can you prepare the training materials and schedule the live session for next week? We'll use A2 (quick-start guide) as the basis.

Yes, I'll prepare the training materials by end of this week. I'll include slides on the workflow, workspace navigation, and template usage. I'll schedule the live session for Monday next week, assuming TechCorp confirms by then.

One thing to consider: the workspace needs to be configured before training. T6 (configure pilot workspace) should be done before the live training session. Can we make sure the workspace is ready by Friday so teams can explore it during training?

Good point. So sequence: T6 (configure workspace) by Friday, training materials ready by Friday, live training Monday. 98050 will own T6. I'll coordinate with IT to make sure the workspace is set up and accessible.

I can help with T6. I'll create the folder structure, upload the templates, and set up the checklists. I'll also create a 'getting started' document in the workspace so teams know where to find things.
I'll follow up with TechCorp today. Hoping to confirm by EOD so we can lock D7 and move forward with the timeline.

Perfect. So timeline: 83011 confirms TechCorp by EOD today, we lock D7. 14637 and I configure T6 by Friday. 119847 prepares training materials by Friday. Live training Monday. Pilot onboarding starts Monday or Tuesday. This keeps us on track for the 21-day deadline.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results, adjust process, and agree on rollout plan.

messages.text: Sharing the pilot onboarding summary report. TechCorp onboarding completed successfully over the past two weeks. We've captured feedback from the internal team and the customer. A7 summarizes outcomes, issues, and recommendations. A4 shows the KPI snapshot: cycle time was 12 days (target was 14), zero rework cycles, and one minor compliance flag that was caught and corrected. Overall, the pilot was successful, but we have some adjustments to make before broader rollout.

Great results. I'm reviewing A7 now. I see a few issues flagged: (1) the 'setup' phase took longer than expected because the customer had questions about data protection, (2) the workspace structure was confusing for the customer success team initially, (3) one template was missing a required field. Are these the main things we need to fix?

Yes, those are the main issues. For (1), we need to add more detail to the data protection section of A2 (quick-start guide). For (2), we should simplify the workspace structure—maybe consolidate some folders. For (3), we need to update the template in A5. These are all fixable. Let's discuss each one.

I can fix the template issue right away. I'll review A5 and add the missing field. For the workspace structure, I'd suggest we consolidate the 'setup' and 'kickoff' folders into a single 'project setup' folder. That might reduce confusion.

Good idea. I'll update A2 with more detail on data protection and add a section on workspace navigation. I'll also update A6 (workspace structure) to reflect the consolidated folders. These changes should address the main issues from the pilot.
I have a question on the KPIs. A4 shows cycle time was 12 days, but was that with or without the customer's delays? I want to make sure we're measuring the right thing for the rollout.

Good question. The 12 days includes customer delays (they took 2 days to respond to a data protection question). For the rollout, we should track both: internal cycle time (time our team spends) and total cycle time (including customer response time). I'll update A4 to show both metrics.

That makes sense. So D9 is: update A2 with data protection detail, update A5 with missing template field, consolidate workspace folders in A6, and update A4 to track both internal and total cycle time. Once these updates are done, we can move to D10 (go/no-go for rollout).

Agreed. Timeline: 14637 fixes A5 by EOD today, 119847 updates A2 and A6 by tomorrow, I'll update A4 by tomorrow. Once all updates are done, we'll review and lock D9. Then we can decide on D10 (rollout timing).
I'll fix A5 today. I'll also create a change log documenting what was updated and why, so teams know what changed from the pilot version.
Good idea on the change log. I'll do the same for A2 and A6. That way, teams can see what changed and understand the rationale.
One thing to consider for rollout: do we need to update the IT request (A8) or workspace configuration (T6) based on the pilot feedback? Or are the changes just to the guides and templates?

Good question. The workspace consolidation (A6) might require a small IT change, but nothing major. 95041, can you review the A6 updates and confirm with IT that the consolidated structure is still feasible? If there are any issues, let me know.
I'll review the A6 updates and check with IT. Shouldn't be a problem, but I'll confirm by tomorrow.

Perfect. So once all updates are done and IT confirms, we lock D9. Then for D10, we need to decide: do we roll out to all new customers immediately, or do we do a phased rollout? And what's the timeline?

I'd suggest a phased rollout. Start with new customers in the next two weeks, then expand to existing customers who are in early onboarding stages. This gives us time to monitor and adjust if needed. We can make a final decision on D10 once we see the updated materials.

Good plan. So D10 is: phased rollout starting with new customers in the next two weeks. We'll monitor KPIs and adjust as needed. Once all updates are done and reviewed, we'll finalize D10 and close out this project. Timeline: updates by tomorrow, review by EOD tomorrow, D9 and D10 locked by end of week.
